title: Inherency
subtitle: Stock Issues · Mission 07
tagline: Why hasn't the problem been fixed yet? Learn how to show that the **status quo** (the way things are now) can't fix it — and why your **plan** has to.

slides.headline: Why hasn't anyone {{cyan: already fixed it}}?
body: You stand at the briefing table. Your team has a new **plan** — let's say, free Wi-Fi in every school. A debater on the other team raises a hand:

quote.text: If it's such a good idea, why hasn't it happened yet? What's stopping it right now?

slides.definition: The reason the problem is {{amber: still there right now}} — and why it {{cyan: won't go away}} without your plan.
slides.plainWords: What's *stopping* the fix from happening on its own?
slides.analogy: A door that's stuck. Before you can prove your crowbar will open it, you have to show *why* it's stuck.

slides.headline: Three Types of Inherency
slides.intro: Every **Affirmative** case uses at least one of these. The type you pick changes your whole game plan.

cards.name: STRUCTURAL
cards.description: A **law or rule** blocks the fix.

example.label: EXAMPLE
example.text: "A federal law says no — so nothing changes unless Congress changes the law."

cards.name: ATTITUDINAL
cards.description: **What people think or feel** blocks the fix.

example.label: EXAMPLE
example.text: "Voters won't pay for mental health programs because they don't see them as important."

cards.name: EXISTENTIAL
cards.description: No system **exists yet** to deal with the problem.

example.label: EXAMPLE
example.text: "Right now, no government group is watching AI to keep it safe."

prompt.label: SCENARIO INTERCEPT
prompt.scenario: A debater's **Aff** case says: *"Schools should ban smartphones. Right now, parents and teachers can't agree on a rule, so nothing gets done."*
prompt.question: Which type of inherency is this?

options.text: Attitudinal — people can't agree, so nothing changes
Existential — no system for it exists at all
This isn't inherency — it's a harm

correct.title: ✓ TARGET ACQUIRED
body: Correct — this is {{amber: attitudinal}} inherency. There's no law in the way; the thing blocking the fix is that people can't agree. When humans don't agree, the plan doesn't move.
correct.followup: **Tactical note:** Attitudinal cases are strong but tricky. **Neg** will try to argue that people can change their minds on their own — with no plan needed.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: Not quite. The right answer is {{cyan: B — Attitudinal}}. No law is stopping a school from making a phone rule. What's stopping it is people not agreeing — and that's attitudinal.
wrongDefault.followup: **Quick check:** If you took away the people and how they feel, would the block still be there? If no → it's attitudinal.

prompt.label: FIELD ASSESSMENT
prompt.question: Sort each statement into the correct inherency type.

cards.text: "A federal rule says you can't sell raw milk across state lines."
"Most voters won't raise the gas tax, even though it would pay to fix the roads."
"No country has signed any treaty about cleaning up space junk."
"The Constitution says you need a 2/3 vote to do this."

correct.title: ✓ ALL TARGETS SORTED
body: Nice work, debater. Spotting the type of inherency fast — in the middle of a round — is what makes a strong debater stand out.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ MISPLACEMENT
body: That one isn't in the right bin. Re-read the card and try again — the type comes from *what's doing the blocking*.

slides.headline: How Neg attacks {{amber: your}} Inherency
slides.intro: If you know what's coming, you can build a stronger case. Here are the three moves a smart **Neg** debater will use on you:

rows.name: "It's already happening"
rows.description: Neg shows that the status quo is *already* fixing the problem — so no plan is needed.

counter.label: YOUR COUNTER
counter.text: Bring new **evidence** that the fix is too slow or too small to count.

rows.name: "It would happen anyway"
rows.description: Neg says the thing in the way is about to go away on its own — a new bill, a court ruling.

counter.label: YOUR COUNTER
counter.text: Show that the same block has been there for years, and past "fixes" stalled out.

rows.name: "Wrong block"
rows.description: Neg agrees something IS in the way — but says it's a different thing than you named, and your plan doesn't deal with it.

counter.label: YOUR COUNTER
counter.text: Be specific. Name the exact law, attitude, or missing system you're fixing.

prompt.label: FULL ENGAGEMENT
prompt.scenario: An **Aff** debater says: *"The U.S. should require background checks at gun shows. Right now, federal law has a gap that lets private sellers skip the check — so a lot of guns get sold with no check at all."*
prompt.question: What's the BEST **Neg** attack on this Inherency?

options.text: "The problem isn't big enough to matter."
"Your plan doesn't fit the resolution — that's topicality."
"21 states have already closed this gap — the status quo is fixing it."
"Background checks don't actually stop gun violence."

correct.title: ✓ TARGET ACQUIRED
body: Correct — this is the classic "{{amber: it's already happening}}" attack. By showing that 21 states have already closed the gap, **Neg** says the status quo is fixing it on its own — no federal plan needed.
correct.followup: **How to counter:** Show that the other 29 states still have the gap, or show that a federal fix would work in a way the state fixes can't.

a.title: ✕ WRONG STOCK ISSUE
body: That attacks **significance**, not inherency. Significance is about *size of the harm*. Inherency is about *what's keeping the problem here*.

b.title: ✕ WRONG STOCK ISSUE
body: That's a **topicality** move — it argues the plan doesn't fit the resolution. Not an inherency attack.

d.title: ✕ WRONG STOCK ISSUE
body: That attacks **solvency** — whether the plan actually fixes the problem. Solvency comes later in the stock issues. Inherency asks *why* the problem is still here.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ MISFIRE — RECALIBRATE
body: The right answer is {{cyan: C}}. The question asks for an *inherency* attack. The others attack different **stock issues** — strong moves, just not inherency moves.
wrongDefault.followup: **Key idea:** Inherency attacks are always about *why the problem is still here* — or whether it really is.

slides.headline: MISSION COMPLETE
slides.subtext: You've got {{cyan: Inherency}}. The sector opens up.
